title: Configure software to have secure settings by default
reason: The secure-defaults baseline (docs/security/SECURE-DEFAULTS.md) records what the AWS stacks and the site set to secure values by default (PW.9.1), each item with the stack line that sets it and the test that fails if it is removed (PW.9.2): every bucket private with all four public-access blocks, owner-enforced, encrypted (SSE-S3) and refusing requests not over TLS; the media read only by its CDN, which serves HTTPS only with TLS 1.2 minimum; tower-data not publicly accessible, encrypted, with IAM authentication and deletion protection; no inbound security group but the database's from the tasks; a permissions boundary on every role; the site's session cookies HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure over HTTPS, its CSRF and origin checks on and its auth and admin routes rate-limited. Partial: the site's content security policy only reports (Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, with 'unsafe-inline' scripts), the site sets no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy header, and its Lambda and front door are not defined in this tree's stacks, so no test here proves what they add. Since 19/11 the site enforces its CSP and sends HSTS, nosniff, a referrer policy and frame denial (seen live); it stays partial while script-src allows unsafe-inline (no nonces yet) and the site Lambda and its front door stay outside this tree's stacks.
